description: NEBLUX es un equipo independiente de Pamplona, Colombia, apasionado por la ciencia, la tecnología y la exploración espacial. Inspirados en la neblina de nuestra ciudad y la luz del conocimiento, buscamos transformar desafíos en soluciones innovadoras. Nos interesan la inteligencia artificial, la programación, el análisis de datos y la investigación científica. Valoramos la creatividad, el pensamiento crítico y el trabajo en equipo para generar soluciones de impacto.
summary:
We developed Neblux: Lunar Mission Commander, an educational browser-based simulator that allows children around the age of 10 to manage a lunar base with four astronauts. Across five missions, players manage energy, air, water, and food, protect the crew from radiation, and tackle a Mars exploration scenario.

We address the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning the systems needed to live beyond Earth into playable decisions. A custom simulation engine calculates the consequences and generates forecasts to compare strategies. The experience combines an interactive 3D base, guides, and questions, drawing on NASA references while clearly distinguishing them from educational assumptions.

NEBLUX matters because it allows players to explore an idea that is difficult to grasp through explanations alone: in space, resources are limited, and all systems are interconnected. Its purpose is to spark scientific curiosity and encourage systems thinking through experimentation and learning from decisions.
details:
NEBLUX: Lunar Mission Commander is a browser-based educational simulator in which children around the age of 10 take command of an experimental lunar base for four astronauts. Their goal is to keep the crew alive and manage resources while discovering how the systems that support life beyond Earth are interconnected.

What it does and how it works

The experience unfolds through five missions: recycling water and caring for a crop; managing the battery during an energy crisis; resolving a malfunction that increases CO₂ levels; protecting the crew during a solar storm; and dealing with a dust storm and communication delays on Mars.

Players decide which equipment to activate, how to distribute resources, and when to act. A custom simulation engine developed in JavaScript progressively updates energy, oxygen, CO₂, water, crop conditions, and simulated radiation exposure. These systems are interconnected: a decision about electricity consumption can affect other processes essential to the crew.

The same engine generates forecasts to anticipate the consequences of maintaining a particular configuration. Players can observe a problem, adjust their strategy, and compare results. After completing each mission, they receive up to three stars, review an explanation, and answer questions about what they have learned.

Benefits and expected impact

NEBLUX aims to develop systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and the ability to make decisions with limited resources. It allows players to experiment, make mistakes, and try again while observing the consequences in an educational environment.

Its intended impact is to support classroom and outreach activities focused on space exploration, sustainability, and technology. The connections among water, energy, food, and habitability also encourage reflection on resource conservation on Earth. Evaluation with students and teachers is planned as a next step to study its contribution to learning and improve the experience.

Tools and technologies

We use JavaScript with ES modules for the logic and simulation engine; Three.js to render the base in 3D; Phaser for a fallback 2D view; and the Web Audio API to synthesize sounds. Vite builds the project, and Vitest supports automated testing. Cloudflare Pages hosts the application, while Pages Functions and D1 manage optional user accounts.

Claude, through Claude Code, assisted with programming, writing, and test creation. ChatGPT assisted with generating conceptual illustrations and documentation. The team defined the concept, missions, and development decisions. During gameplay, the game uses programmed calculations and rules, without artificial intelligence.

No specialized hardware or installation is required. Players can access the game on a computer, tablet, or mobile phone and select “Play without an account.”

Creativity of the proposal

NEBLUX’s creativity lies in turning scientific relationships into decisions that players can explore through experience. The base follows a conceptual architectural proposal inspired by the shell of the olive ridley sea turtle. Its four modules represent life support and habitability, radiation protection, energy, and food production. ODY-R, a Basset Hound-shaped exploration robot, gives the experience a distinctive identity.

The combination of conceptual architecture, interactive visualization, and simulation allows players to explore the base and understand the purpose of its equipment.

Factors considered and methodology

We considered the target audience’s age, instructional clarity, difficulty, compatibility across devices, and access without registration. Easy mode uses faces, bars, and short messages; expert mode displays numerical values and graphs.

Development included problem definition, documentary research, conceptual design, model construction, implementation, and integration. The simulator was tested against mission requirements, including its controls, indicators, and responses to player decisions.

We also considered scientific transparency. We use NASA references and distinguish them from educational assumptions. Crop growth times, equipment capacities, and radiation representation are simplified to make the experience understandable. NEBLUX is an educational model; its fictional base is not an engineering design, and the project is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by NASA.
